semin-durr:3-3.t:
His saying: {إِلاَّ قَلِيلاً نِّصْفَهُ}: People have said a great deal about this, and have used it as evidence for the permissibility of excepting the majority and the half, with objections and replies to them. Here I set it out in a refined form, with the help of Allah the Exalted.

Know that this verse has eight possible analyses. The first: that «نصفَه» is a badal (substitute) for «الليلَ», a partial substitute of the whole (badal baʿḍ min kull), and «إلاَّ قليلاً» is an exception from the half, as if it were said: "Stand less than half of the night." The pronoun in «مِنْه» and «عليه» refers back to the half.

The meaning is a choice between two matters: between standing less than half the night definitively, and choosing one of two options, namely reducing from the half or adding to it. Al-Zamakhsharī said this. The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) objected to him, saying that it entails repetition in the wording, since the implied form becomes: "Stand half the night except a little of the half of the night, or reduce from the half of the night." He said: "This is a construction from which the Quran is to be held free." I say: The analysis is problematic, though not for this reason, for the matter here is easy, but for another reason [which I shall mention shortly, Allah willing].

Abū al-Baqāʾ judged this analysis to be the less preferred, for he said: "The second is that it is a badal from «قليلاً», meaning the half." He said: "And it is closer to the apparent sense of the verse, because He said: «أو انقُصْ منه أو زِدْ عليه», and the hāʾ in both refers to the half. If the exception were from the half, the implied form would be: 'Stand half the night except a little, or reduce from it a little', and the little that is excepted is not determined, so reducing from it is not conceivable." I say: The reply to this is that some of them have determined this little: from al-Kalbī and Muqātil, it is the third, so the little was not undetermined. Moreover, there is a contradiction in his statement, for he said, "The little that is excepted is not determined, so reducing from it is [inconceivable]," thus returning the pronoun to the little, whereas in the first instance he returned it to the half.

Someone might say: This analysis can be struck by a strong problem: that it entails repetition of one and the same meaning. For his saying "Stand half the night except a little" has the sense of "reduce from the night", because that little has the sense of reduction; and if you say "Stand half the night except the little of the half" and "Stand half the night, or reduce from the half", you will find the two to have one meaning. There is subtlety in this, so reflect on it. Al-Ḥawfī mentioned no analysis other than this first one, so you now know what is in it.

Among those who held it was Abū Isḥāq (al-Zajjāj), who said: "«نصفَه» is a badal from «الليل», and «إلاَّ قليلاً» is an exception from the half. The pronoun in «منه» and «عليه» refers to the half. The meaning: Stand half the night, or reduce from the half a little, down to the third, or add to it a little, up to the third, or add to it a little, up to the two-thirds. So it is as though He said: Stand two-thirds of the night, or its half, or its third."

I say: The implied forms that they bring out are clear and good, except that the construction does not support them, because of the problem I mentioned to you above.

The second: that «نصفَه» is a badal from «قليلاً». Al-Zamakhsharī, Abū al-Baqāʾ and Ibn ʿAṭiyya held this. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you wish, you may make «نصفَه» a badal from «قليلاً», and it is then a choice among three: between standing the half in full, standing less than it, and standing more than it. He described the half as 'little' only in relation to the whole." I say: This is what Abū al-Baqāʾ judged closer than making it a badal from «الليل», as stated above.

However, the Shaykh objected to this and said: "If «نصفَه» is a badal from «إلاَّ قليلاً», then the pronoun in «نصفَه» either refers back to the substituted-for word (mubdal minhu) or to the one from which the exception is made, namely «الليلَ». It cannot refer to the substituted-for word, because it would then be an exception of something unknown from something unknown, the implied form being: 'except a little, half of the little', and this has no valid meaning at all. If the pronoun refers to «الليل», there is no benefit in making the exception from «الليل», since it would be shorter, clearer and further from confusion to say: 'Stand the night, half of it.' We have already refuted the view of whoever said that «إلاَّ قليلاً» is an exception from the badal, namely «نصفَه», and that the implied form is: 'Stand the night, half of it, except a little of it,' that is, of the half. Moreover, in the claim that «نصفَه» is a badal from «إلاَّ قليلاً» with the pronoun in «نِصفَه» referring to «الليل», there is the application of 'little' to the half, and it also entails that the implied form becomes: 'except its half, so do not stand it, or reduce from the half that you do not stand', and this is a meaning that is not valid and is definitely not what the verse intends."

I say: We hold that the pronoun may refer to either of them, and no objectionable consequence follows. As for what he mentioned, that it would be an exception of something unknown from something unknown, this is rejected; rather it is an exception of something known from something known, for we have shown that the little is a specific quantity, namely the third, and the night is not unknown. Moreover, the exception of an indefinite quantity has occurred. Allah the Exalted said: {مَّا فَعَلُوهُ إِلاَّ قَلِيلٌ مِّنْهُمْ} [al-Nisāʾ: 66]. And He said: {فَشَرِبُواْ مِنْهُ إِلاَّ قَلِيلاً مِّنْهُمْ} [al-Baqara: 249]. [Translator's note: the next clause is as printed in the source:] He should have said: because it is a badal of something unknown from something unknown. As for what he mentioned, that a shorter and clearer wording is "such and such": the shorter is conceded; that it is confusing is rejected. He departed from the wording he mentioned only because it is more eloquent.

By this analysis, those who said that excepting the half and the majority is permissible have argued. The point of the evidence for the first is that it made «قليلاً» an exception from «الليل», and then explained that little as the half, as if it were said: "Stand the night except its half."

The point of the evidence for the second is that it conjoined «أو زِدْ عليه» to «انقُصْ منه», so it has excepted what exceeds the half, because the pronoun in «مِنْه» and in «عليه» refers to the half. This is weak evidence, because the greater quantity came only through conjunction. It is like your saying: "I owe him ten except five, and a dirham, and a dirham." The excess over the half arises by way of conjunction, not because the exception itself removed the majority.

The third: that «نصفَه» is also a badal from «الليلَ», as in the first analysis, except that the pronoun in «منه» and «عليه» refers to what is less than the half. Al-Zamakhsharī held this, for he said: "If you wish, you may say: since the meaning of {قُمِ الليل إِلاَّ قَلِيلاً نِّصْفَهُ}, when you make the half a badal from «الليل», is 'Stand less than half the night', the pronoun in «منه» and «عليه» returns to the less than half. It is as though it were said: 'Stand less than half the night, or stand less than that lesser amount, or a little more than it,' so the choice, beyond the half, is between it and the third."

The fourth: that «نصفَه» is a badal from «قليلاً» as stated above, except that you make the second «قليلاً» a quarter of the night. Al-Zamakhsharī also clarified this, saying: "When you make «نصفَه» a badal from «قليلاً» and explain it by that, you may make the second «قليلاً» mean half of the half, that is, the quarter, as if it were said: 'or reduce from it a little, its half,' and make the addition to this little, I mean the quarter, half of the quarter, as if it were said: 'or add to it a little, its half.' It is also possible to make the addition, being unrestricted, the completion of the third, so the choice is between the half, the third and the quarter." End of quotation. These analyses that I have related from Abū al-Qāsim (al-Zamakhsharī) bear witness to the breadth of his knowledge of the Book of Allah. When his expression proved too broad for the Shaykh, he said: "How wide is this man's imagination! He allows what is near and what is far." I say: What would it have cost the Shaykh to say: "How wide is this man's knowledge!"

The fifth: that «إلاَّ قليلاً» is an exception from the standing, so that you take «الليل» as a generic noun and then say «إلاَّ قليلاً», that is, except the nights whose standing you leave because of a clear excuse and the like. This view is good if one holds that the command is recommended (nadb). Ibn ʿAṭiyya said it, as a possibility of his own. In his wording it was "those in which you fall short of standing," and I replaced it with "those in which you leave standing." In sum, this goes against the apparent sense and is a remote interpretation.

The sixth: al-Akhfash said: "The original is: 'Stand the night except a little, or its half.'" He said: "Like your saying: 'Give him a dirham, two dirhams, three,'" that is, "or two dirhams or three." This is very weak, because it involves omitting the conjunction, which is not allowed; only something anomalous has occurred, which can be interpreted, such as their saying: "I ate meat, fish, dates." And the other's saying:

4364 - كيف أَصْبَحْتَ كيف أَمْسَيْتَ مِمَّا ... يَزْرَعُ الوُدَّ في فؤادِ الكريم
(Gloss: "How did you wake, how did you spend the evening" is among the things that plant affection in the noble heart.)

meaning: meat and fish and dates, and likewise "how did you wake and how did you spend the evening". People have analysed this as badal al-badāʾ.

The seventh: al-Tabrīzī said: "The command to stand, with the choice of adding and reducing, applies to the two-thirds from the end of the night, because the first third is the time of the ʿatama (the early part of the night after dusk). The exception comes upon what is commanded, so it is as though He said: 'Stand two-thirds of the night except a little,' that is, less than its half, 'or add to it,' that is, to the two-thirds. So the choice of adding and reducing applies to the two-thirds." This is a strange statement that does not emerge from this construction.

The eighth: that «نصفَه» is accusative by the implication of a verb, that is, "stand its half". Makkī related it from others, for he said: "«نصفَه» is a badal from «الليل»; it is also said that it is accusative by the implication of 'stand its half'." I say: In reality this is the very badal analysis he mentioned first, because a badal is on the intention of repeating the governing word.

semin-durr:5-5.t: His saying: {إِنَّا سَنُلْقِي}: This clause is resumptive (mustaʾnafa). Al-Zamakhsharī said: "This verse is a parenthetical (iʿtirāḍ)." Then he said: "By this parenthesis he meant that the night standing he was charged with is among the heavy and difficult obligations with which the Quran came, because the night is the time of rest, repose and stillness, so whoever keeps it alive must oppose his own nature and strive against his soul." End of quotation. He means "parenthetical" in terms of meaning, not in terms of the technical craft (of grammar); that is because His saying {إِنَّ نَاشِئَةَ الليل هِيَ أَشَدُّ} corresponds to His saying {قُمِ الليل}, so it resembles a parenthesis in that it enters between these two corresponding statements.

semin-durr:6-6.t:
His saying: {إِنَّ نَاشِئَةَ الليل}: There are several analyses of «الناشئة». The first: that it is an adjective of an omitted noun, that is, "the soul that arises in the night," which rises from its bed for worship, that is, gets up and rises. It is from "the cloud arose (nashaʾat)" when it rose, and "he arose (nashaʾa) from his place" and "nashaza" when he got up. He said:

4365 - نَشَأْنا إلى خُوْصٍ بَرَى نَيَّها السُّرى ... وأَشْرَف منها مُشْرِفاتِ القَماحِدِ
(Gloss: We rose toward sunken-eyed camels whose fat the night-travel had worn away, while their high-standing parts towered above.)

The second: that it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) meaning standing at night, being a maṣdar of «نَشَأَ» when he stood and rose, so it is like «العافية». Both were said by al-Zamakhsharī.

The third: that it is in the language of the Abyssinians; "the man nashaʾa" means he stood at night. The Shaykh said: "On this, it is the plural of «ناشِىء», that is, one who stands" [Translator's note: the source text repeats "that is, one who stands" here, an apparent printing duplication]. I say: He means that it is an adjective for something that conveys plurality, that is, a group or a company that arises; otherwise, a fāʿil form is not pluralised as fāʿila.

The fourth: that «ناشئة الليل» are its hours, because they arise one after another. Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḥasan restricted them to what comes after the ʿishāʾ, and what is before it is not nāshiʾa. ʿĀʾisha, may Allah be pleased with her, specified it in another sense: that it be after sleep, so if no sleep preceded it, it would not be nāshiʾa.

His saying: {وَطْأً}: Abū ʿAmr and Ibn ʿĀmir read it with kasra on the wāw and fatḥa on the ṭāʾ, followed by an alif (wiṭāʾan). The rest read it with fatḥa on the wāw and sukūn on the ṭāʾ. Qatāda and Shibl, on the authority of the people of Mecca, read «وِطْئاً». The apparent sense of Abū al-Baqāʾ's words suggests that it was read with fatḥa on the wāw with lengthening, for he said: "«وِطاء» with kasra on the wāw means muwāṭaʾa (agreement); with fatḥa it is a noun for the maṣdar; and «وَطْئاً» is on the pattern faʿl, and is the maṣdar of «وَطِىءَ»." So «الوِطاء» is the maṣdar of «واطَأَ», like «قِتال», the maṣdar of «قاتَل». The meaning: it is stronger in agreement, that is, the heart of the soul agrees with its tongue, if you mean the soul; or the heart of the one standing agrees therein with his tongue, if you mean the standing or the worship or the hours; or it is stronger in conformity with what is intended of humility and sincerity. And «الوَطْء» with fatḥa or kasra in the sense: firmer in footing and further from slipping; or heavier and harsher on the one praying than the prayer of the day, from his saying, peace be upon him: "O Allah, press down Your tread upon Muḍar." And on every analysis, its accusative status is as tamyīz (specification).

His saying: {وَأَقْوَمُ}: Al-Zamakhsharī related: "That Anas read «وأَصْوَبُ قِيلاً», and it was said to him: 'O Abū Ḥamza, it is only «وأقومُ»!' He said: 'Aqwam, aṣwab and ahyaʾ are the same.' And that Abū Sirār al-Ghanawī read «فحاسُوا خلالَ الديارِ» with the unpointed ḥāʾ, and it was said to him: 'It is with jīm.' He said: 'Ḥāsū and jāsū are the same.'" I say: He has a purpose in these two reports, namely the permissibility of reciting the Quran by meaning, but there is no evidence in this, because it is an explanation of meaning. Moreover, what we have before us is a mutawātir Quran, and this report is a single-chain report (āḥād). It has already been mentioned that Abū al-Dardāʾ used to teach men to recite {إِنَّ شَجَرَةَ الزقوم طَعَامُ الأثيم} [al-Dukhān: 44], and the man kept saying: "al-yatīm." When he grew weary of him he said: "The food of the wicked (al-fājir), you there." Those who hold that it is permissible used this as evidence for it. There is no evidence in it, because Abū al-Dardāʾ's aim [was] to explain the meaning, so he brought a clarifying expression.

semin-durr:7-7.t:
His saying: {سَبْحَاً}: The majority read it with the unpointed ḥāʾ, and it is the maṣdar of «سَبَحَ». It is a metaphor: swimming in water, which is going far in it, is borrowed for the busy handling of one's needs. Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar, ʿIkrima and Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «سَبْخاً» with the pointed khāʾ. They differed in its explanation. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is a metaphor from «سَبْخ الصُّوف», which is to fluff it and spread out its parts, for the spreading of worry and the scattering of the heart by distractions. It is also said: «التَّسبيخ» means lightening. Al-Aṣmaʿī related: «سَبَخَ الله عَنَك الحُمَّى», that is, He lightened it for you. The poet said:

4366 - فَسَبِّخْ عليكَ الهَمَّ واعلمْ بأنَّه ... إذا قَدَّرَ الرحمنُ شيئاً فكائِنُ
(Gloss: Lighten your worry, and know that when the Merciful decrees something, it will come to be.)

that is, lighten. From it comes «لا تُسَبِّخي بدُعائِك», that is, do not lighten. It is also said: «التَّسْبيخ» is stretching. One says «سَبِّخي قُطْنَكِ», that is, stretch it out, and «السَّبيخة» is a piece of cotton; the plural is «سبائخ». Al-Akhṭal said, describing a hunter and dogs:

4367 - فأَرْسَلوهُنَّ يُذْرِيْنَ الترابَ كما ... يُذْرِيْ سبائخَ قُطْنٍ نَدْفُ أوتارِ
(Gloss: They sent them off, scattering the dust as the carding of bowstrings scatters tufts of cotton.)

Abū al-Faḍl al-Rāzī said: "Ibn Yaʿmar and ʿIkrima read «سَبْخاً» with the pointed khāʾ and said: its meaning is sleep, that is, he sleeps by day so as to seek help from it for standing at night. This reading may bear a meaning other than this, but the two explained it, so there is no going beyond it." I say: This needs consideration, because the most that can be said is that the two transmitted this reading and its explanation appeared to them to be as they stated, and it does not follow from that that an explanation of the word other than what they mentioned is impermissible.

semin-durr:8-8.t:
His saying: {تَبْتِيلاً}: It is a maṣdar not on the pattern of its verb (maṣdar ʿalā ghayr al-maṣdar), standing in the place of «التَّبَتُّل», because the maṣdar of «تَفَعَّل» is like «تَصَرَّفَ تَصَرُّفاً» and «تكرَّمَ تكرُّماً», whereas «التفعيل» is the maṣdar of «فَعَّل», like «صَرَّف تَصْرِيفاً». Similar is the poet's saying:

4367 - وقد تَطَوَّيْتُ انْطِواءَ الحِضْبِ
(Gloss: I have coiled myself up as the male snake coils.) [Translator's note: the verse number 4367 repeats the number given to the previous verse in the preceding entry, as printed in the source; only a single hemistich is quoted.]

So he put the form of inflection (infiʿāl) in the place of the form «التَّفَعُّل». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Because the meaning of «تَبَتَّل» is «بَتَّلَ نفسَه», so it was brought on its meaning, out of regard for the rhyme-endings of the verses (fawāṣil)." «التبتُّل» is severance. From it comes «امرأة بتولٌ», that is, a woman cut off from marriage, and «بَتَلْتُ الحَبْلَ» means I cut the rope. Al-Layth said: «البَتْلُ» is the separation of one thing from another. They said: «طَلْقَةٌ بَتْلَةٌ» and «هِبَةٌ بَتْلَةٌ», meaning its being cut off from its owner. So «التبتيل» is abandoning marriage and being abstinent about it. What is meant by it in the noble verse is devotion to the worship of Allah the Exalted without abandoning marriage. In the hadith: "that he forbade tabattul," that is, severance from marriage; from it the monk is called «مُتَبتِّلاً» because of his severance from marriage. Imruʾ al-Qays said:

4368 - تُضِيْءُ الظلامَ بالعَشِيِّ كأنَّها ... منارةُ مُمْسَى راهِبٍ مُتَبَتِّلِ
(Gloss: She lights up the darkness in the evening as though she were the lamp-tower of a celibate monk's evening quarters.)

semin-durr:9-9.t:
His saying: {رَّبُّ المشرق}: The two (al-Kisāʾī and Ḥamza), Abū Bakr (Shuʿba from ʿĀṣim) and Ibn ʿĀmir read «ربِّ المشرق» in the genitive, as an adjective of «ربِّك», or a badal from it, or a clarification of it. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "And from Ibn ʿAbbās, it is as an oath, with the particle of oath omitted, like your saying «اللَّهِ لأفعلَنَّ», and its answer is {لاَ إله إِلاَّ هُوَ}, as you say «واللَّهِ لا أحدَ في الدار إلاَّ زيدٌ»." The Shaykh said: "Perhaps this analysis is not sound from Ibn ʿAbbās, because it involves omission of the preposition, which the Basrans permit only with the glorified name Allah specifically; and because a negated nominal clause in the answer to an oath is negated only by «ما» alone, and «لا» negates only a clause beginning with an imperfect verb, commonly, or with a past verb in its sense, rarely, as in his saying:

4369 - رِدُوا فواللَّهِ لا ذُذْناكُمُ أبداً ... ما دام في مائنا وِرْدٌ لوُرَّادِ
(Gloss: Come to the water, for by Allah we will never drive you off, as long as there is any watering left for the waterers in our water.)

Al-Zamakhsharī brought that by way of allowing it and conceding it, and what the grammarians mention is its negation with «ما», as in his saying:

4370 - لَعَمْرُك ما سَعْدٌ بخُلَّةِ آثمٍ ... ولا نَأْنَأٍ يومَ الحِفاظِ ولا حَصِرْ
(Gloss: By your life, Saʿd is no friend of a sinner, nor a weakling on the day of defence of honour, nor one who is constrained.)

I say: Shaykh Jamāl al-Dīn Ibn Mālik stated without restriction that a negated clause, whether nominal or verbal, is answered with «ما», «لا», or «إنْ» in the sense of «ما», and this is the apparent position.

The rest of the Seven read it in the nominative, as a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is the clause {لاَ إله إِلاَّ هُوَ}, or as the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, that is, "He is the Lord of". This is better, for the connection of the speech with one another. Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «رَبَّ» in the accusative, as praise (madḥ). The majority read «المَشْرِقِ والمغربِ» in the singular, whereas ʿAbd Allāh (ibn Masʿūd) and Ibn ʿAbbās read «المشارِقِ والمغارِبِ». In Zayd's reading it is also possible to make «ربَّ» accusative in two other ways. One of them: that it is a badal from «اسمَ ربِّك», or a clarification of it, or an adjective of it, as Abū al-Baqāʾ said, and this follows from the view that the name is the thing named. The second: that it is accusative by ishtighāl (preoccupation) with an implied verb, that is, "so take the Lord of the East and the West, so take Him," and what is between them is parenthetical.

semin-durr:11-11.t:
His saying: {والمكذبين}: It may be accusative as mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment), which is the apparent sense, and it may be accusative by conjunction (nasaq), which is more consistent with the craft of grammar.

His saying: {أُوْلِي النعمة}: It is an adjective (naʿt) of «المكَذِّبين». «النَّعْمَةُ» with fatḥa means living in comfort; with kasra, bestowing favour; with ḍamma, delight. One says «نُعْمُ» and «نُعْمَةُ عَيْنٍ».

His saying: {قَلِيلاً}: It is an adjective of a maṣdar, that is, "a respite (tamhīlan)", or of an omitted adverb of time, that is, "a short time".

semin-durr:12-12.t:
His saying: {أَنكَالاً}: It is the plural of «نِكْل». There are two views on it; the better known is that it is the shackle (qayd). It is also said to be the iron collar (ghull), but the first is better known. Al-Khansāʾ said:

4371 - دَعاكَ فَقَطَّعْتُ أنكالَهُ ... وقد كُنَّ مِنْ قبلُ لا تُقْطَعُ
(Gloss: He called you, so I cut his shackles, though before that they could not be cut.)

semin-durr:13-13.t:
His saying: {ذَا غُصَّةٍ}: «الغُصَّةُ» is the shajā, that is, what lodges in the throat and cannot be swallowed. One says «غَصَصْتَ» (with kasra), so you are «غاصٌّ» and «غَصَّانُ». He said:

4372 - لو بغيرِ الماءِ حَلْقي شَرِقٌ ... كنتُ كالغَصَّانِ بالماءِ اعتصاري
(Gloss: Had my throat choked on something other than water, I would be like the one who chokes on water, seeking relief in it.)

semin-durr:14-14.t:
His saying: {يَوْمَ تَرْجُفُ}: There are several analyses of it. The first: that it is accusative by «ذَرْني», which is remote. The second: that it is accusative by the "settling" (istiqrār) to which «لَدَيْنا» is attached. The third: that it is an adjective of «عذاباً», attached to an omitted word, that is, "a punishment occurring on the day when the earth quakes". The fourth: that it is accusative by «أليم». The majority read «تَرْجُفُ» with fatḥa on the tāʾ and ḍamma on the jīm, active voice; Zayd ibn ʿAlī reads it in the passive, from «أَرْجَفَها».

His saying: {مَّهِيلاً}: Its original is «مَهْيُول» like «مَضْروب». The ḍamma on the yāʾ was found heavy, so it was moved to the preceding quiescent letter, the hāʾ, and two quiescent letters met. The grammarians differed about what to do in that case. Sībawayh and his followers dropped the wāw, and it was the more fitting to drop because it is the additional letter, even though the rule is that what is dropped when two quiescent letters meet is the first; they then put kasra on the hāʾ so that the yāʾ is sound, and its pattern is then «مَفِعْل». Al-Kisāʾī, al-Farrāʾ and al-Akhfash dropped the yāʾ, because the rule when two quiescent letters meet and one of them must be dropped is that the first is dropped; by their view it should have been said «مَهُوْل», except that they put kasra on the hāʾ for the sake of the yāʾ that had been there, and the wāw was turned into yāʾ; its pattern is then «مَفُوْلاً» in the original form and «مَفِيلاً» after the change.

Makkī said: "All of them allowed it to come in its original form in speech, so you say «مَهْيُوْل» and «مَبْيُوع» and the like, among the roots with yāʾ. If it is of the roots with wāw, it is not allowed to come in its original form according to the Basrans, while the Kufans allowed it, as in «مَقْوُوْل» and «مَصْوُوْغ». All of them allowed «مَهُوْل» and «مَبُوْع» according to the dialect of those who say «بُوع المتاعُ» and «قُوِل القولُ», and the difference over what is dropped from it is as stated above." I say: Completing the form in «مَبْيُوع» and «مَهْيُوْل» and their like is the dialect of Tamīm, and dropping is the dialect of the rest of the Arabs. One says: «هِلْتُ الترابَ أَهيلُه هَيْلاً» so it is «مَهِيل». There is also a dialect: «أَهْلتُه» as a quadriliteral verb, «إهالةً», so it is «مُهال», like «أبَعْتُه إباعَةً» so it is «مُباعٌ».

«والكثيبُ» is what is gathered of sand. The plural of paucity is «أَكْثِبَة», and of multitude «كُثْبان» and «كُثُب», like «رَغِيف», «أرْغِفَة», «رُغْفان», «رُغُفُ». Dhū al-Rumma said:

4373 - فقلت لها: لا إنَّ أهليَ جيرةٌ ... لأكثبةِ الدَّهْنا جميعاً وماليا
(Gloss: I said to her: No, my family are neighbours of the dunes of al-Dahnāʾ, all of them, and so is my property.)

«والمَهيلُ» is what pours down under the foot, that is, spills, from «هِلْتُ الترابَ», that is, I threw it down. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "From «كَثَبْتُ الشيءَ» when you gather it, and from it «الكُثْبةُ» of milk. The ewe said: I am shorn in fleeces and milked in quick small portions."

semin-durr:16-16.t: His saying: {فعصى فِرْعَوْنُ الرسول}: He made it definite only because it was mentioned earlier. This is the lām of previous reference (al-ʿahdiyya). When the Arabs mention a noun first and then report about it a second time, they bring it definite with «أل», or bring its pronoun, so that it is not confused with another, for example "I saw a man, and I honoured the man," or "and I honoured him." If you said "and I honoured a man," it would be thought that he was not the first. The verification of this will come at His saying {إِنَّ مَعَ العسر يُسْراً} [al-Sharḥ: 6] and his saying, peace be upon him: "One hardship will never overcome two eases."

semin-durr:17-17.t:
His saying: {يَوْماً}: It is accusative either by «تَتَّقُون» as a direct object, loosely speaking. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«يوماً» is a direct object, that is: how will you protect yourselves on the Day of Resurrection, and its terror, if you remain in disbelief?" The Shaykh disputed it and said: "«تَتَّقون» is the imperfect of «اتَّقى», and «اتَّقى» does not have the meaning of «وَقَى» so as to be explained by it; «اتَّقى» takes one object, and «وَقَى» takes two. Allah the Exalted said: {وَوَقَاهُمْ عَذَابَ الجحيم} [al-Dukhān: 56]. For that reason al-Zamakhsharī implied it as «تَقُون أنفسَكم», but «تَتَّقون» does not have the meaning of «يَقُوْن», so it is not made transitive in its manner." End of quotation.

It is also possible that it is accusative as an adverbial (ẓarf), that is: how will you manage piety on the Day of Resurrection if you disbelieved in the world? Al-Zamakhsharī said it. It is also possible that it is accusative as a direct object of «كَفَرْتُمْ» if «كَفَرْتُمْ» is taken in the sense of «جَحَدْتُم» (you denied), that is: how will you fear Allah and be in awe of Him if you deny the Day of Resurrection? It cannot be accusative as an adverbial, because they will not disbelieve on that day; rather they will certainly believe. It is also possible that it is accusative by removal of the preposition, that is, "if you disbelieved in the Day of Resurrection". The majority read «يوماً» with tanwīn and make the clause after it its adjective. The returning pronoun is omitted, that is, "it makes the children grey-haired on it". Abū al-Baqāʾ said it, and did not address the agent of «يَجْعل»; on this it is the pronoun of the Creator, the Exalted, that is, "a day on which Allah makes..." Better than this is to make the returning pronoun latent in «يَجْعَلُ», being its agent, and the attribution of making to the day is by way of exaggeration, that is, the day itself makes the children grey-haired.

Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «يومَ يَجْعَلُ», with the adverbial annexed to the clause. The agent on this is the pronoun of the Creator, the Exalted. The "making" here means "turning into", so «شِيْباً» is the second object, and it is the plural of «أَشْيَب». The original of the shīn is with ḍamma, but it was given kasra so that the yāʾ is sound, like «أحمر» and «حُمْر». The poet said:

4374 - مِنَّا الذي هُوَ ما إنْ طُرَّ شارِبُه ... والعانِسُون ومنا المُرْدُ والشِّيْبُ
(Gloss: Among us is he whose moustache has not yet sprouted, and the unmarried grown men; among us are the beardless youths and the grey-haired.)

And another said:

4375 - . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... لَعِبْنَ بنا شِيْباً وشَيَّبْنَنا مُرْدا
(Gloss: [first hemistich missing in the source] They played with us when we were grey-haired, and they turned us grey when we were beardless.)

semin-durr:18-18.t:
His saying: {السَّمَآءُ مُنفَطِرٌ بِهِ}: It is another adjective, that is, "split open because of its terror." The adjective was not made feminine for one of several reasons. Among them: that «السماء» is interpreted in the sense of «السَّقْف» (the roof). Among them: that it is on the basis of relation (nasab), that is, "possessing splitting," like «مُرْضِعٍ» and «حائضٍ». Among them: that it may be masculine or feminine; al-Farrāʾ recited:

4376 - ولو رَفَعَ السَّماء إليه قوماً ... لَحِقْنا بالسَّماءِ وبالسَّحابِ
(Gloss: Had the sky raised any people up to it, we would have reached the sky and the clouds.)

Among them: that it is a generic noun (ism jins) distinguished from its singular by the tāʾ, so one says «سَماءة»; it has already been mentioned that a generic noun can be both masculine and feminine. For this reason al-Fārisī said: "It is like His saying {جَرَادٌ مُّنتَشِرٌ} [al-Qamar: 7], {الشجر الأخضر} [Yā Sīn: 80] and {أَعْجَازُ نَخْلٍ مُّنقَعِرٍ} [al-Qamar: 20]," meaning that it came in one of the two permissible forms. The bāʾ in it is causal (sababiyya), as stated above. Al-Zamakhsharī allowed it to be the bāʾ of instrumentality (istiʿāna), for he said: "The bāʾ in «به» is like it in your saying «فَطَرْتُ العُوْدَ بالقَدُومِ فانْفَطر به»" (I split the wood with the adze, and it split by it).

His saying: {وَعْدُهُ}: The pronoun may refer to Allah the Exalted, even though no mention of Him has preceded, because it is known, so the maṣdar is annexed to its agent. It may also refer to the day, so it is annexed to its object. The agent, which is Allah the Exalted, is then implied.

semin-durr:20-20.t:
His saying: {مِن ثُلُثَيِ الليل}: The majority read with ḍamma on the lām, which is the original, like «الرُّبُع» and «السُّدُس»; Hishām read it with sukūn for lightness.

His saying: {وَنِصْفَهُ وَثُلُثَهُ}: The Kufans and Ibn Kathīr read both in the accusative, and the rest read both in the genitive. In the genitive there is a difficulty, as will come. The accusative is a conjunction (nasaq) upon «أَدْنى», because it has the sense "a time nearer (adnā)", that is, closer; nearness was borrowed for closeness of distance in time. This corresponds to the division at the beginning of the sūra: if he stands less than two-thirds of the night, it is true of him that he stood the night except a little, because the time in which he did not stand would be the third and something of the two-thirds, so His saying «إلاَّ قليلاً» is true of him. As for His saying «ونِصْفَه», it corresponds to His first saying «نِصْفَه». As for His saying «وثُلُثَه», His saying {أَوِ انقص مِنْهُ} may bring the reduction, in the case of the little, to the point where the time is two-thirds of the night. As for His saying {أَوْ زِدْ عَلَيْهِ}, when he adds a little to the half, the time is less than the two-thirds. So it corresponds to "less than two-thirds of the night", and His saying {نِّصْفَهُ أَوِ انقص مِنْهُ قَلِيلاً} is an explanation of the indefinite thing indicated by His saying {قُمِ الليل إِلاَّ قَلِيلاً}. On the accusative reading, al-Ḥasan explained «تُحْصُوه» as "you are able for it".

As for the genitive reading, its meaning is that the standing varies: at one time less than two-thirds, at another less than half, at another less than a third; that is because it is impossible for people to know the measure of time given the excuse of sleep. Al-Zamakhsharī clarified all this, saying: "«نصفَه وثلثَه» was read in the accusative, meaning that you stand less than two-thirds, and stand the half and the third; this corresponds to the choice mentioned at the beginning of the sūra: between standing the half in full, standing less than it, which is the third, and standing more than it, which is the less than two-thirds. It was read in the genitive, that is, you stand less than two-thirds and less than the half and the third, and it corresponds to the choice between the half, which is less than the two-thirds, and the third, which is less than the half, and the quarter, which is less than the two-thirds and the third, which is less than the half, and the quarter, which is less than the third, and this is the last analysis." [Translator's note: the source text repeats this list in garbled form, as printed.] End of quotation. By "the last analysis" he means the interpretations he put forward at the beginning of the sūra.

Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Fāsī said: "In the accusative reading there is a difficulty, unless one implies: its half at one time, its third at another, and less than the half and the third at another, so the meaning is sound."

His saying: {وَطَآئِفَةٌ}: It is nominative by conjunction upon the pronoun in «يقومُ»; the separation by the adverbial and what is conjoined to it permitted that.

His saying: {والله يُقَدِّرُ الليل}: Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Putting His name, the Mighty and Majestic, first as a mubtadaʾ upon which «يُقَدِّرُ» is built is what indicates the sense of exclusivity in determining."

The Shaykh disputed this and said: "If it were said «زيدٌ يحفظُ القرآن», that would not indicate his exclusivity." He took the exclusivity in the verse to be understood from the context, not from what he mentioned.

His saying: {أَنْ لَنْ} and «أَنْ سيكونُ»: both are lightened forms of the heavy «أنّ», and the separator is the negation and the particle of extension (sīn).

His saying: {وَآخَرُونَ}: It is conjoined to «مَرْضَى», that is, He knew that there would be found among you a group who are sick and another group who are travelling. So «يَضْرِبون» is an adjective of «آخرون», and likewise «يَبْتَغون». It is also possible that «يَبْتَغون» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent of «يَضْرِبون», and «آخرون» is conjoined to «آخرون», and «يقاتِلون» is its adjective.

His saying: {هُوَ خَيْراً}: The majority read «الخير» in the accusative, as a second object. «هو» is either emphasis of the first object or a separator (faṣl). Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed it to be a badal, which is a mistake, because it would have to agree with what precedes it in case-ending, so one would say «إياه». Abū al-Sammāl and Ibn al-Samayfaʿ read «خيرٌ», so that «هو» is a mubtadaʾ and «خيرٌ» its khabar. The clause is the second object of «تَجِدوه». Abū Zayd said: "It is the dialect of Tamīm; they put in the nominative what comes after the separator." Sībawayh recited:

4377 - تَحِنُّ إلى ليلى وأنتَ تركتَها ... وكنتَ عليها بالمَلا أنتَ أَقْدَرُ
(Gloss: You long for Layla when it was you who left her, and when you were in the open country you were the more able over her.)

The rhymes are nominative. It is also transmitted as «أقْدَارا» in the accusative. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«هو» is a separator, and it is allowed even though it does not fall between two definites, because «أَفْعَلَ مِنْ», in its refusal of the definite article, resembles a definite." I say: This is the well-known view. Some of them allow it with indefinites other than «أفعل».

semin-durr:1-1.t:
His saying: {المزمل}: Its origin is «المتزَمِّلُ», and the tāʾ was assimilated into the zāy. One says «تَزَمَّل يتزَمَّلُ تَزَمُّلاً» ("he wrapped himself up"). When assimilation is intended, the connecting hamza (hamzat al-waṣl) is brought in, and Ubayy ibn Kaʿb read according to this original. ʿIkrima read «المُزَمِّل» with a light zāy and a doubled mīm, as an active participle. On this there are two views. One: that its origin is «المُزْتَمِلُ», on the pattern مُفْتَعِل, then the tāʾ was changed to mīm and assimilated; this was said by Abū al-Baqāʾ, and it is weak. The other: that it is an active participle of «زَمَّل» with doubling, and on this the object is omitted, that is, "the one who wraps his body." It was also read so, except with fatḥa on the mīm, as a passive participle of it, that is, "the one wrapped up." التَّزَمُّل means wrapping oneself. One says «تَزَمَّلَ زيدٌ بكساءٍ», that is, he wrapped himself in a cloak. Dhū al-Rumma said:
4362 - وكائِنْ تَخَطَّتْ ناقتي مِنْ مَفازةٍ ... ومِنْ نائمٍ عن ليلِها مُتَزَمِّلِ
(How many a desert has my she-camel crossed, and how many a sleeper, wrapped up, heedless of his night.) And Imruʾ al-Qays said:
4363 - كأنَّ ثبيراً في أفانينِ وَدْقِه ... كبيرُ أُناسٍ في بِجادٍ مُزَمَّلِ
(As though Thabīr, amid the varieties of its rain, were the chief of a people wrapped in a striped cloak.) This is like the reading of some mentioned above. In the exegesis it is said that he was addressed so because of his wrapping himself in a cloak.

semin-durr:2-2.t: His saying: {قُمِ الليل}: The majority read the mīm with kasra, because of the meeting of two silent letters. Abū al-Sammāl read it with ḍamma, following the vowel of the qāf. It was also read with fatḥa, seeking lightness. Abū al-Fatḥ said: "The aim is to escape the meeting of two silent letters, so with whichever vowel the first is moved, the aim is achieved." I say: except that the original is kasra, for a reason the grammarians mentioned. «الليلَ» is an adverbial (ẓarf) for the standing, even if the event occurring in it spans all of it. This is the statement of the Basrans; as for the Kufans, they make this kind a direct object.
